library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Du_2024_nivolumab_ipilimumab_imae"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Du_2024_nivolumab_ipilimumab_imae"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13070> (open access; Appendix S1
  carries the baseline table and the model-selection tables)

Du 2024 pooled 3507 patients from 15 nivolumab, ipilimumab and nivolumab plus
ipilimumab studies to ask whether the higher exposures that adolescents
(12 to < 18 years) reach on the adult dosing regimens carry a higher risk of a
grade 2 or higher immune-mediated adverse event (gr2+ IMAE). The model is a
semiparametric Cox proportional-hazards regression of the time to the first
gr2+ IMAE on the time-varying daily average concentrations (daily Cavg) of
both antibodies, their product, and ten baseline covariates, stratified by
treatment (nivolumab monotherapy, ipilimumab monotherapy, nivolumab plus
ipilimumab).

```{r load-model}
imae <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Du_2024_nivolumab_ipilimumab_imae"))
```

The packaged model returns the **relative hazard** `hr` (and its logarithm
`lhr`) against the paper's Figure 1 reference patient. A Cox regression
leaves the baseline hazard unspecified, and this one left three of them
unspecified (one per treatment stratum), so the absolute probability of a
gr2+ IMAE is not a quantity the fit produced. Every check below is therefore
on hazard ratios.

# Population

The analysis set (Appendix S1 Table S1) holds 3507 patients: 42 younger than
12 years, 55 adolescents (12 to < 18 years) and 3410 adults. Median age is 58
years (range 1-90) and median baseline body weight 79.4 kg (9.3-183 kg);
39.2% are female and 96.6% White. The population is mostly melanoma treated
in the advanced (58.3%) or adjuvant (38.6%) setting, with 3.2% other tumour
types or settings, almost all of them pediatric. Treatment was nivolumab
monotherapy in 57.2%, ipilimumab monotherapy in 23.9% and nivolumab plus
ipilimumab in 18.9%, across many weight-based and flat regimens. The endpoint
is the first gr2+ IMAE regardless of immune-modulating treatment; the
ipilimumab-monotherapy studies reported immune-related adverse events, which
were used in their place (Table S2).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Du_2024_nivolumab_ipilimumab_imae")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every coefficient is printed directly in Du 2024 Table 1 on the log-hazard
scale. The model formula is the bold row of Appendix S1 Tables S4 and S5,
`Surv(START, STOP, EVENT) ~ CAVGN * CAVGI + AGE + WTB + LINEM + TTYPEFM +
PDL15M + PSM + SEXM + RACEM + LIBLDHR + strata(TRTP)`.

```{r source-trace, echo = FALSE}

  "e_cav_nivo_haz (CAV_NIVOLUMAB, ug/mL)", "-0.0004655", "Table 1, 'Nivolumab daily C avg'",

  "e_wt_haz (per kg, centred at 75)", "0.006033", "Table 1, 'Body weight'; centring from Figure 1 caption",
  "e_line_2l_haz (1 - LINE_1L)", "-0.2079", "Table 1, 'Line of therapy [>=2L:1L]'",

  knitr::kable()
```

# Helper: evaluating the relative hazard

The model has no ODE and no dose, so a covariate grid is supplied as an event
table with one observation row per scenario; `time` is only an index.

```{r helper}
ref_patient <- data.frame(
  CAV_NIVOLUMAB = 0, CAV_IPILIMUMAB = 0, AGE = 60, WT = 75, LINE_1L = 1,
  TUMTP_MEL_ADJUVANT = 0, TUMTP_OTHER = 0, PDL1_TUM_POS = 0,
  PDL1_TUM_MISSING = 0, ECOG_GE1 = 0, SEXF = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0,
  RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_OTHER = 0, LDHR = 1
)

# One row per scenario: the reference patient with the named columns changed.
scenario <- function(...) {
  x <- ref_patient
  changes <- list(...)
  x[names(changes)] <- changes
  x
}

hr_eval <- function(covs) {
  ev <- cbind(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_len(nrow(covs)), amt = 0, evid = 0L),
    covs
  )
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(imae, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(covs))
  s$hr
}

# Tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit.
half_unit <- function(printed) {
  dec <- nchar(sub("^[^.]*\\.?", "", printed))
  0.5 * 10^(-dec)
}

stopifnot(hr_eval(ref_patient) == 1)
```

# Validation 1: Table 1 hazard ratios and confidence intervals

Table 1 prints each estimate, its standard error and the hazard ratio with a
95% CI computed as `exp(Estimate +/- 1.96 SE)` (Table 1 footnote d). The
check confirms that the packaged coefficients are the printed estimates and
that `exp()` of each reproduces the printed hazard ratio within the rounding
of both printed columns. Only one row needs the estimate's rounding: the
Black/African American row prints 0.7309, while exp(-0.3134) = 0.73096
rounds to 0.7310. The CI bounds use the printed standard errors, which are themselves rounded,
so they are held to 0.1% instead.

```{r table1}
theta <- imae$theta
tab1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~param, ~estimate, ~se, ~hr, ~lo, ~hi,
  "e_cav_nivo_haz", "-0.0004655", 0.0009231, "0.9995", "0.9977", "1.001",
  "e_cav_ipi_haz", "0.007693", 0.003228, "1.008", "1.001", "1.014",
  "e_age_haz", "0.00414", 0.001987, "1.004", "1", "1.008",
  "e_wt_haz", "0.006033", 0.00156, "1.006", "1.003", "1.009",
  "e_line_2l_haz", "-0.2079", 0.09439, "0.8123", "0.6751", "0.9774",
  "e_tumtp_mel_adjuvant_haz", "-0.2972", 0.0889, "0.7429", "0.6241", "0.8843",
  "e_tumtp_other_haz", "0.3119", 0.207, "1.366", "0.9105", "2.05",
  "e_pdl1_pos_haz", "-0.02175", 0.06456, "0.9785", "0.8622", "1.11",
  "e_pdl1_missing_haz", "-0.1229", 0.08553, "0.8844", "0.7479", "1.046",
  "e_ecog_ge1_haz", "0.0877", 0.06695, "1.092", "0.9574", "1.245",
  "e_sexf_haz", "0.3423", 0.05882, "1.408", "1.255", "1.58",
  "e_race_asian_haz", "0.2104", 0.2139, "1.234", "0.8115", "1.877",
  "e_race_black_haz", "-0.3134", 0.4529, "0.7309", "0.3008", "1.776",
  "e_race_other_haz", "-0.3504", 0.2276, "0.7044", "0.4509", "1.101",
  "e_log_ldhr_haz", "-0.0209", 0.04906, "0.9793", "0.8895", "1.078",
  "e_cav_nivo_ipi_haz", "-0.000549", 0.000159, "0.9995", "0.9991", "0.9998"
) |>
  mutate(
    est_printed = estimate,
    estimate = as.numeric(estimate),
    packaged = unname(theta[param]),
    hr_model = exp(packaged),
    lo_model = exp(estimate - 1.96 * se),
    hi_model = exp(estimate + 1.96 * se),
    # Both columns are rounded: half a unit of the printed HR plus the HR
    # change across half a unit of the printed estimate.
    hr_tol = half_unit(hr) + hr_model * half_unit(est_printed),
    hr_ok = abs(hr_model - as.numeric(hr)) <= hr_tol,
    ci_ok = abs(lo_model / as.numeric(lo) - 1) < 0.001 &
      abs(hi_model / as.numeric(hi) - 1) < 0.001
  )

tab1 |>
  transmute(
    param,
    estimate = signif(packaged, 4),
    `HR (model)` = signif(hr_model, 5),
    `HR (Table 1)` = hr,
    `95% CI (from SE)` = sprintf("%.4f-%.4f", lo_model, hi_model),
    `95% CI (Table 1)` = paste0(lo, "-", hi)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Deterministic transcription checks.
stopifnot(
  setequal(tab1$param, names(theta)),
  all(tab1$packaged == tab1$estimate),
  all(tab1$hr_ok),
  all(tab1$ci_ok)
)
```

# Validation 2: Figure 1 covariate effects

Figure 1 is the paper's forest plot of covariate effects against the
reference patient (60-year-old 75 kg white male, first-line advanced
melanoma, ECOG 0, PD-L1 < 5%, LDH at the upper limit of normal). For the
continuous covariates it prints the effect at the 5th and 95th percentiles of
the analysis set. Each row below is evaluated through the packaged model, not
recomputed from the coefficients, so it also exercises the centring, the
`1 - LINE_1L` coding and the natural-log LDH term.

```{r figure1}
fig1 <- bind_rows(
  tibble(effect = "Race [Other:White]", printed = "0.704", covs = list(scenario(RACE_OTHER = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "Race [Black:White]", printed = "0.731", covs = list(scenario(RACE_BLACK = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "Race [Asian:White]", printed = "1.23", covs = list(scenario(RACE_ASIAN = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "Sex [Female:Male]", printed = "1.41", covs = list(scenario(SEXF = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "PS [>0:0]", printed = "1.09", covs = list(scenario(ECOG_GE1 = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "PD-L1 [Missing:<5%]", printed = "0.884", covs = list(scenario(PDL1_TUM_MISSING = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "PD-L1 [>=5%:<5%]", printed = "0.978", covs = list(scenario(PDL1_TUM_POS = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "Tumor type [others:MEL]", printed = "1.37", covs = list(scenario(TUMTP_OTHER = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "Tumor type [adjMEL:MEL]", printed = "0.743", covs = list(scenario(TUMTP_MEL_ADJUVANT = 1))),
  tibble(effect = "Line [>=2nd:1st]", printed = "0.812", covs = list(scenario(LINE_1L = 0))),
  tibble(effect = "Baseline LDH/ULN P05 = 0.57", printed = "1.01", covs = list(scenario(LDHR = 0.57))),
  tibble(effect = "Baseline LDH/ULN P95 = 2.94", printed = "0.978", covs = list(scenario(LDHR = 2.94))),
  tibble(effect = "Body weight P05 = 52 kg", printed = "0.87", covs = list(scenario(WT = 52))),
  tibble(effect = "Body weight P95 = 111 kg", printed = "1.24", covs = list(scenario(WT = 111))),
  tibble(effect = "Age P05 = 19.1 years", printed = "0.844", covs = list(scenario(AGE = 19.1))),
  tibble(effect = "Age P95 = 78 years", printed = "1.08", covs = list(scenario(AGE = 78)))
)
fig1$model <- hr_eval(bind_rows(fig1$covs))
fig1 <- fig1 |>
  mutate(ok = abs(model - as.numeric(printed)) <= half_unit(printed))

fig1 |>
  transmute(
    Effect = effect,
    `HR (model)` = signif(model, 4),
    `HR (Figure 1)` = printed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(all(fig1$ok))
```

All sixteen printed effects are reproduced to their last digit. The P95 LDH
row also pins the logarithm: with log base 10 it would be 0.990, not the
printed 0.978 (the P05 row cannot tell the two apart: 1.005 also rounds to
1.01).

```{r ldh-log-base}
ldh_log10 <- exp(imae$theta[["e_log_ldhr_haz"]] * log10(c(0.57, 2.94)))
stopifnot(abs(ldh_log10[2] - 0.978) > half_unit("0.978"))
round(ldh_log10, 3)
```

The Results text adds one more number: the risk for a 15-year-old is 17%
lower than for a 60-year-old (HR 0.830).

```{r age-15}
hr_age15 <- hr_eval(scenario(AGE = 15))
stopifnot(abs(hr_age15 - 0.830) <= half_unit("0.830"))
round(hr_age15, 4)
```

# Validation 3: the setting contrast in Table 2

Table 2 gives the median predicted probability of a gr2+ IMAE in adults on
nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks, once in the advanced and once in the adjuvant
setting. Within one stratum, proportional hazards give
`S_adj(t) = S_adv(t)^HR`, and because that map is monotone it carries the
median probability straight across. So the two printed medians imply a
hazard ratio, `log(1 - p_adj) / log(1 - p_adv)`, which can be set against the
model's adjuvant-versus-advanced term.

```{r table2-setting}
tab2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~p_adv, ~p_adj,
  "6 months", 0.207, 0.162,
  "1 year", 0.286, 0.225
) |>
  mutate(implied_hr = log(1 - p_adj) / log(1 - p_adv))

hr_adj <- hr_eval(scenario(TUMTP_MEL_ADJUVANT = 1))
tab2 |>
  mutate(
    `model HR` = round(hr_adj, 4),
    `% difference` = round(100 * (hr_adj - implied_hr) / implied_hr, 1)
  ) |>
  rename(
    Time = time,
    `Advanced, adult 240 mg` = p_adv,
    `Adjuvant, adult 240 mg` = p_adj,
    `HR implied by Table 2` = implied_hr
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

stopifnot(all(abs(hr_adj / tab2$implied_hr - 1) < 0.05))
```

The model's 0.743 sits about 2.5% below what Table 2 implies (0.757-0.762).
The printed three-digit rounding of the probabilities explains only part of
that (a range of about 0.757-0.767 at 6 months); the rest is consistent with
the paper's adjuvant simulation using its own exposure draws for the
adjuvant population rather than re-using the advanced-melanoma ones, which
the Methods text allows but does not state.

# Time-varying exposure: an illustration

The exposure terms act through the daily Cavg of each antibody, which changes
over a course of treatment. Du 2024 took these from individual empirical-Bayes
PK predictions of the group's pooled adult and pediatric population PK model,
then unpublished; that model has since been published as Hu 2024 and is
packaged as `Hu_2024_nivolumab` and `Hu_2024_ipilimumab`. The maintainers use
the two Hu 2024 models here, at their typical values, to generate daily Cavg
profiles for three regimens over the first 24 weeks:

* an adult (60 years, 75 kg) on nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks;
* the same adult on nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks
  for four doses (N1I3), then nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks;
* a 15-year-old weighing 40 kg on the same N1I3 induction, then the flat
  240 mg every 2 weeks the paper studies for adolescents of 40 kg or more.

This is a demonstration of how the model is used, not a reproduction of a
published figure: the exposure inputs come from a different (later) report
than the one the hazard model was fitted with.

```{r exposure-profiles}
nivo_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hu_2024_nivolumab"))
ipi_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hu_2024_ipilimumab"))

n_days <- 168L
inf_dur <- 0.5 / 24
obs_grid <- seq(0, n_days, by = 0.5 / 24)

pk_events <- function(dose_times, doses, covs) {
  doses_df <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = dose_times, amt = doses, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "central", rate = doses / inf_dur
  )
  obs_df <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = obs_grid, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L,
    cmt = "central", rate = 0
  )
  bind_rows(doses_df, obs_df) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    bind_cols(covs[rep(1, length(dose_times) + length(obs_grid)), , drop = FALSE])
}

# Daily average = trapezoidal AUC over [d, d + 1] divided by one day.
daily_cavg <- function(time, conc) {
  vapply(seq_len(n_days) - 1L, function(d) {
    k <- time >= d - 1e-9 & time <= d + 1 + 1e-9
    tt <- time[k]
    cc <- conc[k]
    sum(diff(tt) * (head(cc, -1) + tail(cc, -1)) / 2)
  }, numeric(1))
}

solve_cavg <- function(model, events) {
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(model), events = events,
                                     returnType = "data.frame"))
  s <- s[!duplicated(s$time), ]
  daily_cavg(s$time, s$Cc)
}

nivo_cov <- function(age, wt, lbm, combo) {
  data.frame(
    AGE = age, WT = wt, LBM = lbm, CRCL = 90, SEXF = 0, ECOG_GE1 = 0,
    RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0, TUMTP_LYMPH = 0, TUMTP_CNS_PRIM = 0,
    TUMTP_OTHER = 0, CONMED_IPI_1Q3W = 0, CONMED_IPI_3Q3W = combo,
    CONMED_BRENTUXIMAB = 0, CONMED_IPI_ANY = combo
  )
}
ipi_cov <- function(age, lbm) {
  data.frame(
    AGE = age, LBM = lbm, TUMTP_MEL = 1, TUMTP_CNS_PRIM = 0, TUMTP_OTHER = 0,
    CONMED_NIVO_1Q3W = 1, CONMED_NIVO_3Q3W = 0
  )
}

induction <- c(0, 21, 42, 63)
maint_q2w <- seq(84, n_days - 1, by = 14)

profiles <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    regimen = "Adult, nivolumab 240 mg q2w",
    AGE = 60, WT = 75, day = seq_len(n_days) - 1L,
    CAV_NIVOLUMAB = solve_cavg(nivo_pk, pk_events(seq(0, n_days - 1, by = 14), 240,
                                             nivo_cov(60, 75, 55, 0))),
    CAV_IPILIMUMAB = 0
  ),
  tibble(
    regimen = "Adult, N1I3 then nivolumab 240 mg q2w",
    AGE = 60, WT = 75, day = seq_len(n_days) - 1L,
    CAV_NIVOLUMAB = solve_cavg(nivo_pk, pk_events(c(induction, maint_q2w),
                                             c(rep(75, 4), rep(240, length(maint_q2w))),
                                             nivo_cov(60, 75, 55, 1))),
    CAV_IPILIMUMAB = solve_cavg(ipi_pk, pk_events(induction, 225, ipi_cov(60, 55)))
  ),
  tibble(
    regimen = "Adolescent 40 kg, N1I3 then nivolumab 240 mg q2w",
    AGE = 15, WT = 40, day = seq_len(n_days) - 1L,
    CAV_NIVOLUMAB = solve_cavg(nivo_pk, pk_events(c(induction, maint_q2w),
                                             c(rep(40, 4), rep(240, length(maint_q2w))),
                                             nivo_cov(15, 40, 32, 1))),
    CAV_IPILIMUMAB = solve_cavg(ipi_pk, pk_events(induction, 120, ipi_cov(15, 32)))
  )
)
stopifnot(nrow(profiles) == 3 * n_days, all(is.finite(profiles$CAV_NIVOLUMAB)))
```

```{r exposure-plot, fig.cap = "Typical daily Cavg of nivolumab and ipilimumab from the Hu 2024 population PK models, used as the time-varying exposure inputs of the Du 2024 hazard model."}
profiles |>
  pivot_longer(c(CAV_NIVOLUMAB, CAV_IPILIMUMAB), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "cavg") |>
  ggplot(aes(day / 7, cavg, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Daily Cavg (ug/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

The relative hazard is then evaluated day by day. The exposure-only part
holds every baseline covariate at the reference patient; the total also
applies each patient's own age and weight.

```{r hazard-over-time}
hr_cov <- profiles |>
  mutate(.row = row_number())
exposure_only <- hr_eval(
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(hr_cov)), function(i) {
    scenario(CAV_NIVOLUMAB = hr_cov$CAV_NIVOLUMAB[i], CAV_IPILIMUMAB = hr_cov$CAV_IPILIMUMAB[i])
  }))
)
total <- hr_eval(
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(hr_cov)), function(i) {
    scenario(
      CAV_NIVOLUMAB = hr_cov$CAV_NIVOLUMAB[i], CAV_IPILIMUMAB = hr_cov$CAV_IPILIMUMAB[i],
      AGE = hr_cov$AGE[i], WT = hr_cov$WT[i]
    )
  }))
)
hr_time <- hr_cov |>
  mutate(`exposure only` = exposure_only, `exposure + age + weight` = total)

# Nivolumab monotherapy: the exposure term is close to flat (Figure 2b shows
# almost no spread of predicted probability across exposure percentiles).
mono <- filter(hr_time, regimen == "Adult, nivolumab 240 mg q2w")
stopifnot(all(mono$`exposure only` <= 1), all(mono$`exposure only` > 0.9))

# Age and weight alone put the 40 kg 15-year-old at exp(0.00414 * -45 +
# 0.006033 * -35) = 0.672 of the adult reference, an identity of the model.
adol <- filter(hr_time, regimen == "Adolescent 40 kg, N1I3 then nivolumab 240 mg q2w")
stopifnot(all(abs(adol$`exposure + age + weight` / adol$`exposure only` -
                    exp(0.00414 * -45 + 0.006033 * -35)) < 1e-6))
```

```{r hazard-plot, fig.cap = "Relative hazard of a first gr2+ IMAE over the first 24 weeks, against the zero-exposure reference patient. Only ratios within one treatment stratum are meaningful: nivolumab monotherapy and the combination have different, unspecified baseline hazards."}
hr_time |>
  pivot_longer(c(`exposure only`, `exposure + age + weight`),
               names_to = "component", values_to = "hr") |>
  ggplot(aes(day / 7, hr, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~component) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Relative hazard", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

For nivolumab monotherapy the exposure term barely moves the hazard (about
5% at the highest daily Cavg), which is the flat nivolumab exposure-response
of Figure 2b. In combination the picture is set by the interaction. Early in
induction, while nivolumab is still low, the ipilimumab term raises the
hazard slightly; as nivolumab accumulates, the negative product term
outweighs it, and the exposure-driven relative hazard falls below 1, most of
all once flat 240 mg nivolumab maintenance starts while ipilimumab is still
circulating. Within the combination stratum, the fitted surface therefore
gives higher combined exposure a lower, not higher, relative hazard. This is
a property of the linear-interaction form Du 2024 selected by BIC (Table S5).
The paper reads it as a "synergistic effect" and as a relatively flat
combination exposure-response. Do not use it to extrapolate beyond the
exposures in the pooled studies.

For the adolescent, the lower age and weight alone cut the hazard by about a
third, and the higher exposures from flat maintenance dosing do not raise it.
That is the paper's main conclusion: adolescents on the adult regimens are
not predicted to carry a higher immune-mediated safety risk (Table 2,
Figure 3).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No baseline hazard.** The model was fitted as a stratified Cox regression,
  so each treatment stratum has its own unspecified baseline hazard. The
  packaged model returns the relative hazard only, and the cumulative
  probabilities of Table 2, Figure 2 and Figure 3 cannot be simulated from
  it. Figure 2a plots baseline cumulative probabilities for the three strata,
  but its caption describes a reference patient (50 years) that differs from
  Figure 1's (60 years), and a digitised step function would be a construction
  rather than a fitted quantity, so it was not encoded.
* **Centring.** Age and weight are centred at the Figure 1 reference values
  (60 years, 75 kg), and the reference categories are those of Figure 1.
  Centring a Cox model does not change any coefficient; it only fixes what
  `hr = 1` means.
* **Line of therapy coding.** The register's `LINE_1L` is 1 for first line;
  the paper's coefficient is for second or later line against first line, so
  the model applies it to `1 - LINE_1L`. The handling of the 23 patients with
  missing line of therapy is not described.
* **PD-L1.** `PDL1_TUM_POS` marks PD-L1 at or above the paper's 5% threshold;
  the model switches it off when `PDL1_TUM_MISSING = 1`, so the two indicators
  cannot both act.
* **Exposure inputs.** `CAV_NIVOLUMAB` and `CAV_IPILIMUMAB` are daily averages (AUC over
  each calendar day divided by one day) in ug/mL, 0 when the antibody is not
  given. The illustration above takes them from the typical-value Hu 2024
  models with 30-minute infusions and starts nivolumab maintenance three
  weeks after the fourth combination dose; Du 2024 used individual
  empirical-Bayes predictions.
* **Abstract body-weight figure.** The abstract gives "0.84 for BW 52 kg
  versus 75 kg". Table 1, Figure 1 and the Results text all give 0.87 for
  that contrast, which the model reproduces; 0.84 (0.844) is Figure 1's
  age-P05 effect, so the abstract appears to have taken the neighbouring
  value.
* **Figure 2 caption.** The reference patient for Figures 2b and 2c lists
  "BLDHR = 10", which is almost certainly 1 (the Figure 1 and Figure 2a
  reference). The difference matters little here: the LDH term would be
  exp(-0.0209 log 10) = 0.953.
* **Table 2 combination rows.** For the combination regimens with
  nivolumab 480 mg every 4 weeks maintenance, Table 2 prints cumulative
  probabilities that fall from 6 months to 1 year (for example 0.629 then
  0.521 for adults), which a cumulative probability cannot do; those rows
  appear to be misaligned and are not used.
* **Endpoint definition.** For the ipilimumab-monotherapy studies the event is
  an immune-related adverse event, used in place of the IMAE definition
  (Table S2); the ipilimumab-monotherapy baseline hazard absorbs the
  difference.
